$comment: Hand curation of the Kwik Floors Duratek collection for the client preview. Image indexes refer to each product's images array in products.json. Kinds: room | closeup | swatch. 'room' labels feed the alt text. Colour families are a judgement from the photography, not client data; confirm with the client. Size diagrams are deliberately excluded. Descriptions are written for the preview from the swatches and plank formats (no performance claims); replace with the client's copy when supplied. Herringbone finishes come from the herringbone collection (source.herringbone_collection) and set style 'herringbone'. Bathroom photographs and size diagrams are excluded for herringbone, per the imagery rules.

finishes.description: A light, honey-toned oak with soft grain and the odd small knot. It keeps a room bright without looking washed out, and suits kitchens and open-plan spaces well.
Mid-brown oak with darker streaks and plenty of knots. The planks are longer and wider than our standard boards, at 228 × 1492mm, so a large room reads with fewer joins.
The warmest finish in the range: rich amber oak with strong, flowing grain and dark knots. It sits naturally in older houses and in rooms that get a lot of daylight.
Deep charcoal grey with crisp grain lines, and the darkest finish in the range. Put it against white walls, pale cabinetry or concrete and let the contrast do the work.
Golden oak with the splits, knots and colour shifts of reclaimed boards. It comes in our extra-long, wider plank (228 × 1492mm), which suits the aged look.
Brown oak with a cool grey wash and a fair amount of grain movement. If you can't decide between warm and grey, start here.
Pale silver-grey, close to whitewashed. The lightest finish we make, and a good choice for small rooms and bathrooms that need every bit of light.
Caramel oak, warm without tipping into orange, with long, straight grain. It looks right with creams, muted greens and natural materials like rattan and linen.
A soft, slightly olive greige with gentle knots. Quieter than Cartmel and a touch warmer than Skiddaw.
Smoked brown oak with real variation from plank to plank, some lighter and some darker. Extra-long, wider planks (228 × 1492mm) give it the look of a wide-board floor.
Smoky grey-brown with pale grain and darker knots. It works as well with a modern kitchen as it does with exposed beams and a log burner.

Honey oak in a herringbone pattern. Painted bevel edges outline each plank, so the pattern reads clearly across the floor. Rigid SPC core, waterproof, with a 0.55 mm wear layer, Duratek Scratch Shield surface and integrated underlay. Unilin click-lock, floating installation.
